fact: Gabon already has substantial mobile money use, according to Biometric Update.
MADIGIPAIE QR payments let customers pay across participating financial institutions, covering more than 3,273 merchants and 1,382 GIMAC QR codes as of July, authorities said.
GIMAC said that in the first half of 2026 payment institutions and mobile money operators, including those of Gabon, dominate GIMACPAY transaction volumes.
GIMACPAY links 56 banks, 26 microfinance institutions, 16 payment institutions and mobile money operators and 52 aggregators across the CEMAC, which processed 20.3 million transactions in 2025.

L'Union says Madigipaie is a national QR code digital payment platform for transactions between merchants and users, working with several banks, whose rollout to merchants the economy minister asked Libreville's mayor to support on 3 July 2026.
The Ministry of Digital Economy launched digital payment in the TaxiGab network on 28 February 2026 under the Madigipaie programme, so riders pay by mobile money or bank app.
Through the interoperable GIMAC QR codes deployed for Madigipaie, TaxiGab users can pay by mobile money or banking app whatever their financial institution, per the ministry.

The Ministry of Economy reported 4.5 million mobile money accounts at end-2024, 1.6 million active, with operators processing 368.3 million transactions worth CFA4,087 billion in 2024; MaDigiPaie lets citizens pay by mobile money by scanning a GIMACPAY QR code (Ecofin Agency).

MaDigiPaie, launched in Libreville on 9 December 2025, lets citizens pay purchases by scanning a GIMACPAY QR code with their Mobile Money application, with more than 1,000 QR codes already deployed with merchants (GIMAC).
The GIMACPAY QR code can be paid from a Mobile Money application whatever the operator ("quel que soit l'operateur"), according to GIMAC.
AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY, live since July 2020, carries P2P and merchant payments to and from 11 mobile money operators across the six CEMAC states including Gabon.
AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY gives all-to-all interoperability between banks, microfinance institutions and mobile money operators in the six CEMAC states including Gabon.
AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY also provides domestic instant payment functionality connecting banks and mobile money wallets in each CEMAC state, including Gabon.
COBAC's 2025 annual report, as relayed by Ecomatin, counts 744 million payment operations in 2025 through licensed payment institutions (Airtel Money Gabon and Clikpay Gabon).

The CEMAC QR Code standard, launched 29 July 2026 across six states including Gabon, lets a client with a bank account, mobile money wallet or microfinance account pay by scan whatever their institution.
GIMACPAY, the CEMAC card-mobile-transfer ecosystem in service since 2021, processed over sixteen million mobile transactions in 2025.
Moov Gabon issued 1,969,325 transactions worth 68.1bn FCFA and Airtel Gabon 1,950,401 worth 55.8bn FCFA in H1 2026, per GIMAC statistics.
Droit Medias Finance reports payment institutions in the CEMAC execute local transfers onto customers' e-money wallets for inbound remittances.
CLIKPAY offers a smartphone and web payments platform for deposits, withdrawals and utilities in all nine Gabonese provinces, with over 5,000 merchants and agents.
CLIKPAY has integrations with Airtel Money, Moov Money and GIMACPay, according to UNCDF.
Mobile Money is used in Gabon to settle CNSS benefit payments, with amounts at or below 100,000 FCFA paid by Mobile Money only.
The article refers to growing mobile money in Gabon, per Biometric Update.
Gabon's digital economy ministry sources say the Gimac QR code already unifies payment platforms, is interoperable and is compatible with other payment applications.
BEAC says the QR code launched 29 July 2026 lets any bank or microfinance mobile app read any merchant's code regardless of institution or CEMAC country.

Business & Finance International, citing the DGEPF note, reports Airtel Money and Moov Money handled 368.3 million mobile money operations worth FCFA 4,087 billion in 2024, including FCFA 291 billion of payments for goods and services.
Connecting Africa reports that Airtel Money wallets in Gabon receive inbound remittances from 7 August 2025, so the mobile money service is in service.
Moov Africa Gabon Telecom's Moov Money app lets subscribers make local and international financial operations from their phones, as reported on 17 January 2025.
GSMA's October 2026 report says 62% of adults in Gabon hold a mobile money account, so mobile money is in service.
